title: Research on the Safeguard Mechanisms for Urban Low-Carbon Planning in China under the Dual-Carbon Era
content: In the context of China’s dual-carbon goals of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, urban low-carbon planning has become central to achieving sustainable urban transformation. However, its implementation remains hindered by fragmented legal frameworks, weak regulatory coordination, limited incentive mechanisms, and insufficient public participation. This study examines how institutional safeguard mechanisms can enhance the effectiveness and enforceability of urban low-carbon planning. Using a comparative case analysis of representative Chinese cities, it investigates the current institutional arrangements, identifies key governance deficiencies, and explores feasible pathways for systemic improvement. The findings reveal that legal institutionalization, integrated regulatory frameworks, diversified incentive policies, and participatory co-governance are critical to advancing low-carbon planning and ensuring policy coherence. These insights can improve administrative efficiency, enhance stakeholder engagement, and create a resilient governance structure that supports long-term carbon reduction. The study contributes to the theoretical understanding of urban low-carbon governance and provides actionable policy guidance for cities in developing countries pursuing sustainable and inclusive low-carbon transitions under the global climate governance framework.
